clue.text: Perhaps atlas goes after my dad's upset with cover from Ordnance Survey

indicators.note: tells the solver that the first-named piece is placed after the rearranged letters
something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: the cover of a word is its outside, so only the first and last letters of the next word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of Ordnance
an atlas is one example of a book

explanation.surface: A child is cross about a map, though help comes from the national mapping agency.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ordnance Survey is Britain's mapping agency, which makes 'Ordnance Survey' look like one unit; in fact only the outside of Ordnance is used and Survey is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Domesday Book of 1086 was William the Conqueror's great survey of English land and property.

clue.text: Diminish terms for quad bike race including group of motorists

indicators.note: terms are ends, so only the final letter of each of the next two words is kept

parts.note: the last letters of quad and bike

indicators.note: one piece includes another, so the motoring group sits inside the race

parts.note: the TT (Tourist Trophy) is the Isle of Man motorbike race
the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: Someone belittles the language used about an off-road quad race that a motoring club joins.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man TT is a famous motorbike road race; the motoring club goes between its two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To detract is to take away from or lessen the value of something, so it is a synonym for diminish.

clue.text: West maybe assuming Asian country exporting atomic powered device

indicators.note: to assume is to take on, so the first name takes the country into itself

parts.note: Mae West, the Hollywood actress, is one West

indicators.note: a country that exports something sends it out, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: a country in Asia
A is the abbreviation for atomic

explanation.surface: The West takes on an Asian nation that sells nuclear-powered equipment abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' looks like a compass point, but it names an actress whose first name is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine is an apparatus that runs on applied power to do work.

clue.text: Complaint of one from France following introduction to Sooty & Sweep

indicators.note: says that the French word is placed after the opening letter
an introduction is the start, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Sooty
un is French for one
a sweep is a stroke, as of an oar or a cricket bat

explanation.surface: A French visitor grumbles about the British children's puppet show Sooty and Sweep.
explanation.walkthrough: Sooty and Sweep are a glove puppet bear and dog from long-running British children's TV, which makes the pair look like one unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunstroke is an illness brought on by too much sun, and complaint is a common word for an ailment.

clue.text: Right also about this writer

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for also is placed around the writer

parts.note: and is a synonym for also
the setter refers to themself

explanation.surface: The writer is also correct about themself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb meaning to put right.
explanation.definitionFit: To right a wrong is to correct it, and to amend something is likewise to correct it.

clue.text: Skin of beautiful snake in waste container

indicators.note: the skin is the outside, so only the outer letters of the next word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of beautiful
the adder is Britain's venomous snake

explanation.surface: A gorgeous snakeskin turns up in a rubbish bin.
explanation.definitionFit: The bladder is the organ that holds urine, the body's liquid waste, until it is passed.

clue.text: Very active in April for example but not the 1st of May — self-confidence needed

indicators.note: the second word is needed alongside the first, so it is added after
but not means without, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: April is one month of the year

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that is taken

parts.note: the first letter of May
ego is one's sense of self-worth

explanation.surface: Being busy in spring, without the confidence boost of May, calls for belief in yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the go is constantly busy and moving about, the idiom for being very active.

clue.text: Day before and railway union say public supports call to strike

indicators.note: in a down clue a support sits underneath, so this piece comes at the bottom

parts.note: the eve is the day before an event
RY is an abbreviation for railway
a union is one kind of organised body
something out is known or made public

explanation.surface: The day before, a rail union announces that the public backs its call for industrial action.
explanation.definitionFit: Everybody out is the traditional shout from a shop steward calling the workforce to walk off the job.

clue.text: In Rome, see a jerk breaking into vehicle

indicators.note: a burglar breaking into somewhere goes inside it, so these letters go inside the vehicle

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
a tic is an involuntary jerk of a muscle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tourist in Rome watches a thug break into a van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb of sightseeing, but it is the noun: a bishop's seat, here the Holy See.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vatican is the Holy See, the Pope's seat of authority, located within the city of Rome.

clue.text: Delighted former journalist holds key

indicators.note: something that holds another keeps it inside, so the key goes within the former journalist

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, so ex means former
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A retired reporter is thrilled to have kept hold of a key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former journalist' looks like one person, but it splits into two pieces with the key between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Exalted can mean jubilant or elated, in a state of high joy, close to delighted.

clue.text: £500 with 50 per cent off at first as my repair is oddly discounted for ages

definitions.note: an idiom for a long time; the answer usually follows for

indicators.text: with 50 per cent off at first
indicators.note: halving applies to the opening letter read as a Roman numeral, so it is swapped for the numeral worth half

parts.note: a monkey is British slang for five hundred pounds

indicators.note: discounting the odd letters throws away the first, third, fifth and so on, keeping the even ones

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on of these words

explanation.surface: A builder charges five hundred pounds, half price at first, though a repair keeps getting knocked down over a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: MONKEY starts with M, Roman 1000; taking 50 per cent off makes it D, Roman 500, giving DONKEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Donkey's years is an informal British idiom for a very long time, matching the sense of for ages.

clue.text: Person who says things as they are extremely rude and very famous

definitions.text: Person who says things as they are

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of rude
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: A blunt-speaking celebrity is both very rude and very well known.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' reads as an intensifier for rude; it actually keeps only the ends of that word.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist faces facts and describes the world plainly, without idealising it.

clue.text: Man ringing conclusively wrong number back creates resentment

indicators.note: the assembled pieces together make up the result
a ring goes round something, so the man encircles the letter

parts.note: dude is slang for a man

indicators.note: conclusively points to the conclusion of the word, so only its last letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of wrong

indicators.note: going back means reading the abbreviation from right to left

parts.note: NO is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A man who keeps dialling a wrong number finally causes ill feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringing' suggests a telephone call, but it means the man surrounds a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dudgeon is a feeling of offence or deep resentment, mostly heard in 'in high dudgeon'.

clue.text: Film star regularly objects to Elvis changing line to ultimately bed Priscilla

indicators.note: changing one thing to another means swapping out the named letters for new ones
regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter of the next words is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of objects to
taken as written
the El is the elevated railway line in Chicago

indicators.note: ultimately points to the end, so only the last letter of each word is kept

parts.note: the last letters of bed and Priscilla

explanation.surface: A gossip piece about Elvis Presley changing his ways to finally sleep with Priscilla, whom he married.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the line in Elvis is changed; his first letter stays and completes the first name of the star.
explanation.definitionFit: Bette Davis was a Hollywood screen actress, double Oscar winner and one of the great stars of classic cinema.

clue.text: Taking just seconds, Horizon enables Post Office to infiltrate finances deliberately

indicators.note: here it sits in the surface while the two pieces are joined in order
only the second letter of each of the next words is taken

parts.note: the second letters of Horizon and enables

indicators.note: to infiltrate is to get inside, so the abbreviation goes inside the money word

parts.note: a purse is a fund of money, one's finances
PO is the abbreviation for Post Office

explanation.surface: Horizon, the faulty accounting system, let the Post Office raid sub-postmasters' money on purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: Horizon is the flawed Post Office computer system behind the UK's sub-postmaster prosecution scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on purpose means doing it intentionally, which is a synonym for deliberately.

clue.text: Metal and plastic suits a mop

indicators.note: plastic material can be moulded into any shape, so the letters are remoulded

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cleaner chooses a mop made of metal and plastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Metal and plastic' reads like a list of materials; plastic is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Potassium is a soft, reactive alkali metal, element K.

clue.text: Damage done on dropping wine over skirt

indicators.note: the wine goes over the other word, covering it on both sides
dropping the word on means it is removed from the word before

parts.note: taken as written
tent is a deep red Spanish wine, an old crossword favourite
a skirt can be an edging or border, as a rim is

explanation.surface: Spilling wine over a skirt has done harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skirt' suggests clothing, but it is the edge of something; 'over' wraps the wine around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Detriment is harm or loss suffered, so it serves as a noun synonym for damage.

clue.text: Sporting cry of friend in basement of frat house

indicators.note: in puts the friend inside the surrounding letters
the basement is the bottom, and in a down clue that is the last letter

parts.note: the last letter of frat
an ally is a friend
HO is an abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A friend calls out from the cellar of a college fraternity house.
explanation.walkthrough: T and HO together surround ALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Tally-ho is the hunting cry raised on sighting a fox, and fox-hunting counts as a sport.

clue.text: Supply cod slices unwrapped for freezing

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, it says the letters bend into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: unwrapping removes the outer layer, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: slices without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A fishmonger provides cod fillets out of their packaging for the freezer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like the verb to provide, but it is the adverb from supple, meaning flexibly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice-cold describes something extremely chilly, as cold as ice, so it matches freezing.

clue.text: See 13
Mounted policeman discovered rhino is strong swimmer

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means going upwards, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: plod is British slang for a police officer

indicators.note: dis-covered means with its cover taken off, so the outer letters go

parts.note: rhino without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A mounted officer has found that the rhinoceros is a powerful swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounted policeman' looks like an officer on horseback; mounted is a reversal signal and discovered strips the rhino.
explanation.definitionFit: The dolphin is a marine mammal famous for swimming fast and powerfully.

clue.text: Most importantly nurse replaces it in a way that's bent?

indicators.note: one thing replacing another takes its place, so the nurse goes where the pronoun was

parts.note: vitally means crucially, most importantly
EN is an enrolled nurse
taken as written

explanation.surface: Above all, a nurse who swaps things over may be acting corruptly.
explanation.walkthrough: Bent is British slang for corrupt, as in a bent copper.
explanation.definitionFit: Venally means in a corrupt, bribable way, and bent is informal for dishonest or corrupt.

clue.text: Boring advice to maintain moving parts?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a drilled hole, here one sunk for petroleum
second meaning: read as a two-word instruction to lubricate thoroughly

explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' reads as dull, but here it is the noun for a drilled hole; the question mark flags the playful second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil well is a bore sunk to extract petroleum, and the phrase also reads as an instruction to lubricate generously.

clue.text: Full portion of salade niçoise

indicators.note: a portion is only part of the dish, so the letters are a run taken from within the words

parts.note: the run of letters across the two words, cedilla ignored

explanation.surface: A generous helping of the classic tuna and egg salad from Nice.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means heavily loaded or filled, a synonym for full.

clue.text: Old silver coin by piano swapped for pound — it's supposed to be golden

indicators.note: swapped for means taken out and replaced, so two letters make way for one

parts.note: the sixpence was a pre-decimal British coin, originally of silver
X is the multiplication sign, read as by
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: An old silver coin left beside a piano is exchanged for a pound coin, as if gold.
explanation.walkthrough: In SIXPENCE the adjacent X and P give way to L. The definition draws on the proverb 'speech is silver, silence is golden'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb holds that silence is golden, so it is the thing supposed to be golden.

clue.text: Doctor — do I try squeezing tip of lymph gland?

indicators.note: squeezing something in holds it inside, so the letter goes within the words
to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a tip is an extremity, here the far end, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of lymph

explanation.surface: A patient asks a doctor whether to try pressing on a lymph node.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a form of address, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The thyroid is an endocrine gland in the neck that regulates metabolism.

clue.text: Breather in hotel bar at last — drinking beer

indicators.note: something drinking takes it in, so the beer goes inside the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ale is a type of beer

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before

parts.note: the last letter of bar

explanation.surface: Someone resting in a hotel bar near closing time has a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: The beer is drunk by the letters either side of it, so it sits just before the end of bar.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhaler is a device for breathing in medicine, or literally one who breathes in, hence a breather.

clue.text: Casting comic according to Spooner's notes?

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words trade places

parts.note: casting is moulding and comic is funny; swap their first sounds

explanation.surface: Choosing actors for a comedy, as the famously muddled Reverend Spooner might describe it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casting' suggests choosing actors, but it means moulding, as in casting metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Folding money is paper currency, banknotes as opposed to coins.
